status: DRAFT FOR REVIEW. Nothing reads this file yet. Once agreed, code will validate it at start-up like the other ontologies.
about: What kinds of claim Titan verifies, and how each kind is settled. A statement is first split into atomic claims (each a word-for-word span of the original) with the qualifiers attached to it; each atom gets a type and a subtype from this file; the subtype says which sources can settle it, which checks apply, how it typically goes wrong, and how its result is worded. Types are about what is ASSERTED (an event, a quantity, a cause, a judgment), not about the topic. Event subtypes reuse the predicates of company_events.json; source kinds reuse the document types of sources.json. Examples use made-up companies (Northwind, Contoso, Litware, Tailspin, Acme, Fabrikam, Woodgrove) so they can never be mistaken for evidence about a real one.
principles: Code first. Patterns, registries, filings and arithmetic settle what they can; a model is only a judge on a short (atom, quote) pair with fixed labels, and every quote it judges is first found word for word in its source by code.
An atom is checked on its own, and so is each qualifier: a claim is often wrong only in its period, scope, attribution or hedge.
The checked text, its own site and copies of it are never evidence for it.
Absence of evidence is reported with its search scope ('no 8-K Item 5.02 filed since 2026-08-26'), never as 'false'.
A judgment is not called true or false: its grounds are listed (observable indicators), or it is said to be an opinion.
Newer sources supersede older ones for states of the world; for events, the issuer's own document outranks reports about it.
Every verdict says what would settle what is left open.

decomposition.about: How a statement becomes atoms. Code splits on the connectors below; a model may split a compound sentence code cannot, but each atom must be a contiguous word-for-word span of the statement, and the atoms together must cover every checkable word.

split_on.note: only between two clauses that each have a verb

split_on.cues: \b(?:over|because of|due to|amid|after|following|as a result of|citing|driven by|thanks to|led to|resulting in)\b
split_on.note: the event and its cause become two atoms; the cause atom is typed causal
'Jordan Reyes, the chief executive of Contoso, said ...' holds a role atom and a speech atom
a relative clause asserting something is its own atom
a characterising word inside an event claim becomes an evaluative atom

example.statement: Contoso CEO Jordan Reyes resigns over governance failure

qualifiers.label: Time of the claim
qualifiers.effect: fixes when the claim must hold; a state claim is checked at that time, else at today

qualifiers.label: Reporting period
qualifiers.effect: a figure is compared only for the same period (skills/temporal/reporting.py)

qualifiers.label: Scope
qualifiers.effect: a segment's or an adjusted figure is not the company's reported total

qualifiers.label: Who says so
qualifiers.effect: the claim becomes 'X says Y': checked as speech; Y itself is checked only if asked

qualifiers.label: Certainty
qualifiers.cues: \b(?:reportedly|allegedly|is said to|rumou?red|sources say|people familiar|may have|appears to|is believed to|unconfirmed)\b
qualifiers.effect: a hedged claim is verified as 'it is reported', and a verdict never drops the hedge

qualifiers.label: How many
qualifiers.effect: 'most' needs a count over a defined set; 'all' and 'none' are bounded absence or universal claims

qualifiers.label: Precision
qualifiers.effect: the comparison tolerance: 'about $3.7 billion' agrees with 3,678 million; 'more than $4 billion' does not

qualifiers.label: Unit or currency
qualifiers.effect: a figure in another unit or currency is converted only when the source states the rate; else not compared

qualifiers.label: Condition
qualifiers.effect: a conditional claim is checked as announced-with-condition, never as done

qualifiers.label: Negation
qualifiers.effect: the claim asserts an absence or a denial: typed absence, or speech when someone denies

checks.does: the evidence sentence is found word for word in the archived source (as for every claim)
the organisation is resolved to one registrant or domain (SEC list, company site); several matches are said, never chosen
a person's name compared surname first, allowing misspellings and the name used versus the name filed (skills/roles)
amounts compared as amounts: '$3.68 billion' is 3,678 million (skills/statements/figures)
the tolerance the claim's own wording allows ('about', 'more than', the digits written)
the same unit and currency, or a stated conversion
the evidence covers the claim's period, dated by the company's fiscal year (skills/temporal/reporting)
consolidated vs segment, GAAP vs adjusted, region: the same scope or said otherwise
for a state of the world, the newest source wins; an older one is reported as 'true as of <date>'
one holder per role per company at a time (company_events rule)
an event a US registrant must file (8-K items) is looked for in the filings; none within the window is evidence, said with the window
completed after announced; terminated after announced (company_events rule)
announced, agreed, pending, completed or terminated: a claim of completion needs a completion
a search aimed at denials, corrections and the opposite ('<company> denies', 'not', 'correction')
who said it first: the earliest dated source carrying it, and whether later ones only repeat it
a derived figure (margin, growth, ratio) is recomputed from the reported figures it rests on
a comparative names its set (peers, market, index); without one the claim is bounded to the set that could be checked, and said so
an absence or universal claim is checked within a stated scope (sources, period), and the verdict names it
an evaluative term is mapped to observable indicators (indicator_sets below) and those are looked for
does this quote state the atom, in other words? Labels: states | contradicts | related | unrelated. Code has verified the quote; disagreement with code's own match is 'needs review'
does this quote give the cause, and who gives it (the company, a named person, unnamed sources, the writer)? Code finds the candidate sentences by the cause's words

settled_by.registry: an official register settles it alone (SEC company list, a stock exchange listing, a companies registry)
settled_by.issuer_document: the issuer's own document settles it alone (a filing, its release, its site): Tier 1
settled_by.filing: an SEC filing settles it alone, and the absence of a required filing is evidence within its window
settled_by.statements: the company's financial statements read by code settle it (skills/statements)
settled_by.independent_two: two independent sources (not copies of one document), or one Tier 1/2 source (settling.py)
settled_by.attributed: settled as 'reported by X': the strongest attribution found is the verdict; the underlying fact stays open
settled_by.indicators: grounds listed from observable indicators; never called true or false
settled_by.bounded: true or false only within a stated set or scope, which the verdict names
settled_by.said_only: only whether it was said can be verified, not whether it will happen

atom_results.supported: the evidence states it, within its qualifiers
atom_results.contradicted: the evidence states otherwise for the same thing, period and scope
atom_results.not_found: no evidence either way within the search scope
atom_results.qualifier_wrong: the core is right, a qualifier is not (period, scope, unit, hedge, stage)
atom_results.outdated: it held at an earlier time and newer evidence shows it no longer does
atom_results.grounds_listed: an evaluative atom: its indicators, found or not
atom_results.not_checkable: an opinion, a prediction or a claim with nothing observable in it

verdicts.label: Partly corroborated
verdicts.meaning: the core atom is supported; another atom (a cause, a characterisation) is not found

verdicts.label: Misleading
verdicts.meaning: the atoms are true but a qualifier is wrong or a framing atom is unsupported, so the statement as a whole misleads (the right figure for the wrong period; a segment presented as the company; a hedge dropped)

verdicts.label: Outdated
verdicts.meaning: true when first reported, no longer

verdicts.label: Contradicted
verdicts.meaning: the core atom is contradicted by evidence

verdicts.label: Unconfirmed
verdicts.meaning: nothing found either way for the core atom

verdicts.label: Opinion
verdicts.meaning: an evaluative or forward-looking statement: its grounds are listed, it is not called true or false

verdicts.label: Not checkable
verdicts.meaning: nothing in it can be observed

combination_rules.say: name the qualifier and what the evidence gives for it

combination_rules.when: core supported and a causal atom contradicted
combination_rules.say: the event is confirmed; the cause given is contradicted by <source>

combination_rules.when: core supported and a causal or evaluative atom not_found
combination_rules.say: what happened is confirmed; '<span>' is not

combination_rules.when: core supported and an evaluative atom grounds_listed
combination_rules.say: list the indicators found, or 'no filed indicator of <term>'

core_atom: The atom the statement is about: an event's occurrence, a quantity's value, a state's holder. In 'X resigns over Y', the resignation; Y is a causal atom attached to it.

types.label: Attribute
types.definition: A lasting property of an entity: what it is called, where it is, when it began.

subtypes.label: Identifier
subtypes.definition: A code that names the entity: ticker, CIK, ISIN, LEI, registration number.
subtypes.example: Northwind trades on Nasdaq under the ticker NWND.
failure_modes: a parent's or a subsidiary's identifier

subtypes.label: Founding
subtypes.definition: When and by whom the entity was founded or incorporated.
subtypes.example: Contoso was founded in 2007 by Jordan Reyes.
failure_modes: the year a predecessor was founded
a co-founder left out or added

subtypes.label: Headquarters or location
subtypes.definition: Where the entity is based or operates.
subtypes.example: Litware is headquartered in Austin, Texas.
failure_modes: a large office taken for the head office

subtypes.label: Legal name or form
subtypes.definition: The entity's registered name, legal form or former names.
subtypes.cues: \b(?:formerly(?: known as)?|renamed|changed its name|doing business as|d/b/a|a subsidiary of|wholly owned)\b
subtypes.example: Tailspin Inc., formerly Tailspin Toys, changed its name in 2024.

subtypes.label: Industry or listing
subtypes.definition: The industry, exchange or index the entity belongs to.
subtypes.example: Fabrikam joined the S&P 500 in March 2026.
failure_modes: added vs announced to be added

types.label: State at a time
types.definition: Something true at a point in time that can change: who holds a role, who owns what, how many employees.

subtypes.label: Role holder
subtypes.definition: Who holds a role at an organisation.
subtypes.example: Jordan Reyes is the chief executive officer of Contoso.

evidence.how: the officer who certified the latest 10-Q or 10-K (Exhibit 31.1 chief executive, 31.2 chief financial), then 8-K Item 5.02 since (skills/roles)

failure_modes: a title that is not the role (president of a division)

subtypes.label: Ownership or stake
subtypes.definition: Who owns an entity or what share of it.
subtypes.example: Woodgrove holds a 12% stake in Litware.

subtypes.label: Size
subtypes.definition: How many employees, customers, stores or users an entity has.
subtypes.example: Northwind had about 12,000 employees at the end of 2025.
failure_modes: a figure from an earlier year

subtypes.label: Operating status
subtypes.definition: Whether an entity, product or deal is active, closed, bankrupt, acquired, delisted.
subtypes.cues: \b(?:bankrupt|insolvent|delisted|defunct|shut down|ceased operations|went private|acquired by|is now part of|discontinued)\b
subtypes.example: Tailspin filed for Chapter 11 protection in May 2026.

types.label: Event
types.definition: Something that happened (or was announced) at a time. Each subtype maps to company_events predicates, which give its required parts, its key date and its rules.

subtypes.label: Transaction
subtypes.definition: An acquisition, merger, divestiture, spin-off, investment or funding round.
subtypes.example: Contoso completed its $2.1 billion acquisition of Litware on October 1, 2026.
failure_modes: the price including debt vs equity value
a terminated deal reported as done
the wrong buyer in a consortium

subtypes.label: Leadership change
subtypes.definition: An appointment, departure or succession in a senior role or on the board.
subtypes.example: Contoso's chief financial officer, Sam Okafor, will step down on June 30, 2026.

filing_items.5.02: departure or appointment of directors and certain officers (within four business days)

failure_modes: a planned departure reported as done
the effective date taken for the announcement date

subtypes.label: Strategic action
subtypes.definition: A strategic review, restructuring, layoff, partnership or product launch.
subtypes.example: Fabrikam announced it will cut 8% of its workforce.
failure_modes: a percentage of one unit reported as of the company

subtypes.label: Financial event
subtypes.definition: Results reported, guidance issued, a dividend or buyback announced.
subtypes.example: Northwind raised its quarterly dividend to $0.42 per share.
failure_modes: an authorisation reported as a completed buyback

subtypes.label: Legal or regulatory
subtypes.definition: A lawsuit, settlement, fine, investigation, approval or ruling.
subtypes.example: Regulators fined Woodgrove $40 million over data handling.
failure_modes: a proposed fine reported as final
a settlement 'without admitting' reported as an admission

subtypes.label: Other event
subtypes.definition: A dated event no other subtype fits.
subtypes.example: Acme opened its first store in Lisbon in 2025.
failure_modes: the date of the announcement vs the date of the event

types.label: Quantity
types.definition: A figure: reported, derived from others, estimated by a third party, or a market price.

subtypes.label: Reported figure
subtypes.definition: A figure the company reports: revenue, net income, EPS, cash, debt.
subtypes.cues: \b(?:revenue|net sales|sales|net income|net loss|profit|EPS|earnings per share|operating income|cash|debt|assets|EBITDA)\b
subtypes.example: Northwind reported revenue of $3.7 billion for the third quarter of 2026.
failure_modes: a segment reported as the company

subtypes.label: Derived figure
subtypes.definition: A ratio or change computed from reported figures: margin, growth, share of total.
subtypes.example: Contoso's operating margin widened to 24% in fiscal 2026.

subtypes.label: Third-party estimate
subtypes.definition: A figure an analyst, research firm or reporter estimates: market share, market size, valuation, sales of a private company.
subtypes.example: Litware holds about 30% of the market, according to research firm Tailspin Analytics.
failure_modes: one firm's estimate presented as consensus

subtypes.label: Market price
subtypes.definition: A share price, market capitalisation or trading move at a time.
subtypes.example: Fabrikam shares fell 9% on May 4, 2026.
failure_modes: a market cap at another date

types.label: Attributed speech
types.definition: That someone said, wrote or announced something. What is verified is that it was said, by whom, where and when; whether it is true is a separate atom.

subtypes.label: Direct quote
subtypes.definition: Words in quotation marks attributed to a person or organisation.
subtypes.example: "We had a record quarter," said Jordan Reyes, Contoso's chief executive.

subtypes.label: Reported speech
subtypes.definition: What someone said, in other words.
subtypes.example: Contoso's chief executive said demand for its chips exceeds supply.
failure_modes: a stronger claim than what was said

subtypes.label: Position or denial
subtypes.definition: An organisation's stated position, a denial or a refusal to comment.
subtypes.example: Woodgrove denied that it is in talks to sell its payments unit.
failure_modes: 'declined to comment' reported as a denial

types.label: Cause or effect
types.definition: That one thing happened because of another, or led to another. Usually attached to an event or a quantity (the core atom).

subtypes.label: Cause given by the party
subtypes.definition: The reason the company or person itself gives.
subtypes.example: Contoso said the decline was due to lower demand in China.
failure_modes: a cause the company never gave
one of several causes presented as the only one
the writer's inference presented as the company's

subtypes.label: Cause reported by others
subtypes.definition: A reason reporters or unnamed sources give.
subtypes.cues: \b(?:sources say|people familiar|according to (?:people|sources|reports)|reportedly|is said to have)\b
subtypes.example: The chief executive left after a dispute with the board, people familiar with the matter said.
failure_modes: a single report repeated by others presented as many

subtypes.label: Cause inferred
subtypes.definition: A cause the writer draws, not stated by anyone.
subtypes.example: Shares fell as investors worried about governance.

types.label: Judgment
types.definition: A characterisation that is not observed directly: a failure, a crisis, a leader, strong or weak. Checked through observable indicators, never called true or false.

subtypes.label: Characterisation
subtypes.definition: A label for a situation or an entity.
subtypes.example: Contoso is a troubled company after a governance failure.
failure_modes: a label without any observable ground
one indicator presented as a pattern

subtypes.label: Quality or standing
subtypes.definition: How good, big or leading something is, without a measure given.
subtypes.example: Litware is a leading provider of payroll software.
failure_modes: a company's self-description repeated as fact

types.label: Comparison
types.definition: More, less, largest, first, only: true only within a set.

subtypes.label: Comparison
subtypes.definition: One thing more or less than another.
subtypes.cues: \b(?:more than|less than|higher than|lower than|bigger than|smaller than|outpaced|ahead of|behind|twice|half of)\b
subtypes.example: Northwind's revenue grew faster than Contoso's in 2025.

subtypes.label: Superlative or rank
subtypes.definition: The largest, fastest, top-ranked within a set.
subtypes.example: Fabrikam is the largest maker of industrial drones in Europe.
failure_modes: a ranking by one firm presented as fact

subtypes.label: First or only
subtypes.definition: The first to do something, or the only one.
subtypes.example: Tailspin was the first company to ship a solid-state battery scooter.
failure_modes: first in one market presented as first anywhere

types.label: Forward-looking
types.definition: About the future. What can be verified is that it was said, by whom and when; the outcome is checked later, if ever.

subtypes.label: Company guidance
subtypes.definition: A figure or range the company expects.
subtypes.example: Contoso expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $15 to $16 billion.
failure_modes: a range reported as a point

subtypes.label: Plan or intention
subtypes.definition: What an organisation plans or intends to do.
subtypes.cues: \b(?:plans? to|intends? to|will|aims? to|is set to|is expected to|on track to)\b
subtypes.example: Northwind plans to open a factory in Ohio in 2027.

subtypes.label: Prediction by others
subtypes.definition: What analysts, reporters or others expect.
subtypes.example: Analysts expect Fabrikam to return to profit next year.

types.label: Absence or universal
types.definition: That something has not happened, never happened, or holds for all. True only within a stated scope.

subtypes.label: Never or not
subtypes.definition: That something has not happened.
subtypes.example: Woodgrove has never paid a dividend.

subtypes.label: All or none
subtypes.definition: That something holds for every member of a set.
subtypes.example: All of Litware's factories run on renewable power.

types.label: Trend
types.definition: A direction over time: a company's own measure, or a wider movement.

subtypes.label: Entity trend
subtypes.definition: A direction in one entity's figures over several periods.
subtypes.example: Northwind's revenue has grown for eight consecutive quarters.

subtypes.label: Wider trend or consensus
subtypes.definition: A movement in a market or society, or what 'most' people think.
subtypes.example: Adoption of AI coding tools is accelerating across the industry.
failure_modes: one survey presented as the trend

indicator_sets.about: Observable signs a company's governance failed. Found: listed as grounds. None found: 'no filed indicator of a governance failure', never 'false'.

indicators.label: Earlier financial statements can no longer be relied on
A director left citing a disagreement
Going-concern doubt
indicators.signal: 'substantial doubt' about the ability to continue as a going concern

indicators.label: Net losses in recent periods
indicators.signal: net loss in the statements read (skills/statements)

indicator_sets.about: Observable grounds for a claim of leadership. Without a stated measure and set, the claim is an opinion with these grounds.

indicators.label: A named firm's market-share estimate
indicators.signal: a share figure with its source and date

indicators.label: A published ranking
indicators.signal: a rank with the ranking's name and year

indicators.label: The company's own description
indicators.signal: said by the company itself: noted, never counted as independent
